analysis:
The only change in this PR is a documentation addition to docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 1030-1046). It describes a PromptTokenCache in LocalTokenizerBridge that reuses token IDs of prompt pieces, scoped per prefix-cache scope. It also describes ChatTemplateLoopRewrites (linear-time rendering of Gemma 4 and GPT-OSS templates), sampled background comparisons that disable reuse on a mismatch, and the kill switch DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0. The supplied units are the surrounding base text (lines 1216-2016), which is unchanged context, so I reviewed the base text for consistency only and found no security-relevant edits there.

The documented behavior touches a few threat-model areas. T-041 covers the prefix-cache TTFT timing oracle and cross-tenant sharing. The new doc states that reuse never crosses a cache scope, which aligns with the coordinator-authored cacheSalt scoping. A token-ID cache is in-memory only, and the doc claims it adds no on-disk artifact. If the implementation keys by the prefix-cache scope as claimed, it creates no new cross-account channel. A same-account timing oracle remains within the accepted SEC-035 risk.

The source code (PromptTokenCache.swift, ChatTemplateLoopRewrites) was not supplied. So I cannot verify the scope-isolation claim, the memory bounds, the parallel encoding on up to four cores (which could affect availability), or the fidelity of the template rewrites. These are open integration questions for whichever PR carries the code, not findings on this docs-only change. Because the threat model treats cache scope isolation as security-relevant, a later review should confirm that PromptTokenCache keys include the coordinator-authored cacheSalt and that eviction is bounded.

No regression is identified in this change.
